title: Microwaves heat food at 2.45 GHz, and not by resonance
body: It is often said 2.45 GHz is water's resonant frequency. It is not; it is an industrial licence-free band where magnetrons are cheap, chosen so waves penetrate centimetres into food instead of searing only the surface. Water absorbs broadly across frequencies; the standard picked a practical compromise in the 1940s and kitchens inherited it.
source_hint: ISM band allocation history; dielectric heating literature
